answer: THE NAMESPACE LADDER. An identity's answer counts only if it registered its own token namespace: the tick's deployer is on the ledger forever, so one address keeps one personal name and no farm passes one down. The protocol posts T, the count of ticks ever registered, and charges the next registration T times a base burn, so the tenth name costs ten times the first. T never falls, so no head can pre-buy cheap names; a farm's own registrations raise the price of its next one. An honest grove pays the base once; a lagoon of clones drowns in the names they take, and the cheapest lotus sinks.
